ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is an AC voltage source symbol labeled V, and on the right side is a single-phase bridge rectifier circuit composed of four diodes, with the load resistor R connected between the two DC bus lines at the output terminals of the bridge rectifier. Reasoning: The problem gives R = 50 Ω and source voltage v_s(t) = 200 sin(ωt) V. Treating it as an ideal diode bridge rectifier, the voltage across the load resistor is the full-wave rectified waveform v_R(t) = |200 sin(ωt)|. Full-wave rectification does not change the root mean square value, therefore V_R,rms = 200/√2 V. The load power P = V_R,rms^2 / R = (200/√2)^2 / 50 = 400 W.
